- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates upside; add 1–3% to forecast if recent price is rising.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at +5% above immediate prior high if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often misses the rebound; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 2–3 days.
- Model underestimates long-term mean reversion after strong rallies; if sentiment is mixed or slightly bearish, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 5–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over 3+ days, model tends to underestimate true price; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is clearly bearish (≤-0.6) and recent price is trending down; if sentiment is neutral, cap forecast at prior 5-day average.
